BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Threshold note on the Seller's framing.** The Seller's preamble and "Reviewer Efficiency Note" assert that [STANDARD] clauses are "cleared by both sides", "settled at principal level" and "FINAL", and invite us to review only [OPEN] items on the basis that the disclosure and limitation package is accepted. Nothing in our playbook or instructions records any such agreement, and no Amelia Frost written authority exists for any fallback. These labels are the other side's drafting, not instructions to us. I have reviewed every clause against the playbook and treated the [STANDARD] tags as having no effect. The "market context" assertions (10–20% caps, 12–18 months, etc.) are advocacy, not evidence, and do not move our positions.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cl 12.1 – 20% / AUD 4,800,000, marked [STANDARD]/FINAL.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure is only a conditional fallback requiring prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none has been given.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** Cl 12.2 – de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- **Buyer wants:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar (tipping)** recovery once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject on all three limbs.** Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the deductible structure would permanently forfeit the first AUD 250,000 of loss, contrary to playbook.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 – 18 months, plus a sweep that any limitation applies to **all** Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims; 18 months only with Amelia Frost written approval (none given); no all-Claims sweep.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "all Claims" default.** No fallback authority exists, and the sweep would silently drag Title/Tax/IP/indemnity claims into the 18-month window.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright; insert a standalone Fundamental Warranties regime.** Capping title at 20% means we could pay AUD 24m for shares we don't own and recover AUD 4.8m – "administrative simplicity" is no justification.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"; no fraud carve-out anywhere in the package.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Non-negotiable; insert full carve-out.** The playbook states no one may waive this, and a package that purports to limit liability for fraud is both unacceptable and likely unenforceable in any case.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Sch 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records"; [1.4] admits nothing.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject [1.1]–[1.2]; require a "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope" standard, specific disclosures only.** Whole-data-room disclosure combined with the Cl 8.3 knowledge bar would effectively eliminate the warranties.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Cl 8.3 – no claim for any matter of which the Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete blanket exclusion; any seller-side knowledge qualifier must reference named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete Cl 8.3 entirely.** A "discoverable" constructive-knowledge test imputed via advisers converts due diligence into a trap and duplicates the already-rejected general disclosure mechanism.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Cl 3/6.3 – reasonable endeavours only; condition deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure Letter [2] confirms **no final consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied** as at 22 September 2026.
- **Buyer wants:** Condition precedent requiring an **effective** consent **and** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; endeavours standard insufficient for a ~30% revenue customer.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; redraft as a hard CP with "effective consent + satisfaction evidence".** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue, so a consent that can lapse on unmet conditions is worthless to us.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Cl 2/7 – ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure Letter [3] confirms not repaid and no discharge of security in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases delivered at Completion. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval (none given).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; require payout, funds-flow repayment and executed releases as Completion deliverables.** Buying a debt-free company while the bank's security remains on foot post-Completion is incompatible with the debt-free/cash-free bargain, and no authority exists for the post-completion route.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** Funds flow – DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller", not itemised. Disclosure Letter [5] confirms they are absent from the funds flow and silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax) as a specific funds-flow line item or expressly seller-funded; no silent exclusion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; add a line item for AUD 420,000 + on-costs, seller-borne, or deduct as Transaction Expenses.** Completion-triggered bonuses are a liability the Company will owe post-Completion, so "a matter for the Seller" without a mechanism leaves us paying twice.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Cl 11.1 – indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, "considered adequate". Disclosure Letter [4]: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open (not independently verified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Broadened indemnity covering ownership/title defects in the SOW3 materials, third-party claims and remediation cost, preserving the SOW3 payment-and-assignment cure; treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified either way.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as inadequate; broaden the indemnity and require pre-Completion evidence of cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment.** The real exposure is the IP not having transferred at all, not merely the AUD 180,000 fee.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** Cl 4.6/Sch 6 – "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material". Disclosure Letter [6]: link sent to unintended external address, ~1,240 records, access/scope/notification undetermined, no loss stated.
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, completed investigation, pre-Completion updates, cooperation covenant and a specific indemnity for any resulting notification/regulatory/third-party cost; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation; impose preservation/investigation/update covenants plus a specific indemnity, without asserting a breach has occurred.** Neither side can yet say whether this is nothing or an eligible data breach, so the contract must allocate the risk rather than pre-judge it.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure Letter [8] is silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment of timing/scope under DD-008 and DD-011 read together; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Hold open; request term sheets, renewal dates and termination rights before conceding "ordinary course".** The playbook does not treat these as Debt, but the Seller's label is unsupported by its own disclosure.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 "all Claims unless expressly stated"; Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 "all Claims of any nature"; Tax/IP "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment/covenant and specific-indemnity claims each in their own regime; no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the three sweep provisions; insert an express priority clause that general limitations do not apply to Fundamental, Tax, IP, indemnity or covenant claims.** Each sweep is a back-door collapse of the separate regimes we require under N-004, N-011 and N-016.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter [10] concedes this is merely the source relied on and that Buyer verification is incomplete.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence – ASIC extract, constitution, board/shareholder approvals, encumbrance (PPSR) searches, director/authority certificates – not the Seller-supplied internal register.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as proof; require independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence as Completion deliverables, backed by the Fundamental Warranty regime.** A register the Seller controls cannot verify the Seller's own title.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, AUD 250k basket).
- **Buyer wants:** Terms remain OPEN; separate Tax and IP regimes to be negotiated; assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled"; record Tax/IP as expressly OPEN and outside Cl 12.** There is no agreement on these terms and folding them into an 18-month/20% regime would be a major unapproved concession.

---

**Summary for the deal team:** The Seller's package falls short of the playbook on every one of the 16 issues; none of the [STANDARD]/FINAL items should be treated as agreed. The highest-value points to lead with are the fraud carve-out (N-005), the Fundamental/Title regime and category separation (N-004/N-014), the disclosure/knowledge pair (N-006/N-007), and the two Completion-mechanics items that go to whether we actually get a debt-free company with its key customer intact (N-008/N-009). No fallback positions should be offered on cap, time limit or Riverlark without written authority from Amelia Frost.
